*I’d hold shipment for one high-priority bug.*

*P1 — Renewal dates are clamped against the wrong month* — `src/schedule.js:6–7`
The code clamps the anchor using the *source* month’s length, then constructs a date in the *next* month. This both skips renewals and loses the anchor after short months:

| From | Anchor | Expected | Actual |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Jan 31, 2026 | 31 | Feb 28 | Mar 3 |
| Feb 28, 2026 | 31 | Mar 31 | Mar 28 |
| Mar 31, 2026 | 31 | Apr 30 | May 1 |

Clamp against the *target* month’s length instead, preserving the original `anchorDay`. Add regression tests for short-month transitions, leap February, and returning to the original anchor afterward.

*Verification:* All 5 existing tests pass, but a separate calendar check across 2024–2028 found 66 incorrect results out of 1,860 cases.

*One product clarification:* Proration matches the new README’s calendar-month rule, but that means an April 16 signup pays half-price while its first renewal is May 16—not May 1. Confirm that discount is intentional for anniversary billing; I haven’t classified it as a bug because it’s explicitly documented.

Reviewed `main` → `billing-anniversary` at `f73b00d`. No files changed.
